At the end of each verse, the congregation responds, “Thank the LORD for He is good; His loving-kindness is for ever.” See law 439.

On Sukkot, the lulav and etrog are waved, three waves for each word of the verse (except God’s name). On the first word, wave forward, then, on subsequent words, wave right, back, left, up and down respectively. The Leader waves only for the first two verses. The congregation waves each time the first verse is said in response.

en:Festivals/Eiruv Tavshilin:1.en: It is not permitted to cook for Shabbat when a Yom Tov falls on Thursday or Friday unless an Eiruv Tavshilin has been made prior to the Yom Tov. This is done by taking a loaf or piece of matza together with a boiled egg, or a piece of cooked fish or meat to be used on Shabbat. While holding them, say the following:

en:Festivals/Eiruv Tavshilin:2.en: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments, and has commanded us about the mitzva of Eiruv.

en:Festivals/Eiruv Tavshilin:3.en: By this Eiruv may we be permitted to bake, cook, insulate food, light a flame and do everything necessary on the festival for the sake of Shabbat, for us and for all Jews living in this city.

en:Festivals/Eiruv Tavshilin:4.en: For Eiruv Teḥumin see page 304. For Candle Lighting see page 304.

parts.en: We give thanks to You, for You are the Lord our God and God of our ancestors, God of all flesh, who formed us and formed the universe. Blessings and thanks are due to Your great and holy name for giving us life and sustaining us. May You continue to give us life and sustain us; and may You gather our exiles to Your holy courts, to keep Your decrees, do Your will and serve You with a perfect heart, for it is for us to give You thanks. Blessed be God to whom thanksgiving is due.

parts.en: Our God and God of our fathers, bless us with the threefold blessing in the Torah, written by the hand of Moses Your servant and pronounced by Aaron and his sons the priests, Your holy people, as it is said: May the Lord bless you and protect you. May it be Your will. May the Lord make His face shine on you and be gracious to you. May it be Your will. May the Lord turn His face toward you, and grant you peace. May it be Your will.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:54.en: In Shacharit, and in Israel in Shabbat Mincha:

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:55.en: Grant peace, goodness and blessing, grace, loving-kindness and compassion to us and all Israel Your people. Bless us, our Father, all as one, with the light of Your face, for by the light of Your face You have given us, LORD our God, the Torah of life and love of kindness, righteousness, blessing, compassion, life and peace. May it be good in Your eyes to bless Your people Israel at every time, in every hour, with Your peace. Blessed are You, LORD, who blesses His people Israel with peace.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:57.en: Grant great peace to Your people Israel for ever, for You are the sovereign Lord of all peace; and may it be good in Your eyes to bless Your people Israel at every time, at every hour, with Your peace. Blessed are You, LORD, who blesses His people Israel with peace.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:59.en: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart find favor before You, LORD, my Rock and Redeemer.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:60.en: My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from deceitful speech. To those who curse me, let my soul be silent; may my soul be to all like the dust. Open my heart to Your Torah and let my soul pursue Your commandments. As for all who plan evil against me, swiftly thwart their counsel and frustrate their plans. Act for the sake of Your name; act for the sake of Your right hand; act for the sake of Your holiness; act for the sake of Your Torah. That Your beloved ones may be delivered, save with Your right hand and answer me. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart find favor before You, LORD, my Rock and Redeemer.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:61.en: Bow, take three steps back, then bow, first left, then right, then center, while saying:

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:62.en: May He who makes peace in His high places, make peace for us and all Israel – and say: Amen.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:63.en: May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, that the Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days, and grant us a share in Your Torah. And there we will serve You with reverence, as in the days of old and as in former years. Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:64.en: On Friday night, the service continues with "Then the heavens and the earth" on page 358.

parts.en: If the first night of Pesach falls on Shabbat, only the first paragraph is said. On the Seder night many say Full Hallel (page 732) followed by Full Kaddish (page 360).

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:66.en: On the other Yamim Tovim, both in Mincha and Maariv, Full Kaddish (page 360) is said.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:67.en: On the last nights of Pesach, the Omer (page 284) is counted after Full Kaddish (page 360).

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:68.en: On Simchat Torah, both in Maariv and Shacharit say Full Kaddish (page 360), then continue with "You have been shown" and Hakafot on the next page.

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:71.en: On the second day of Shavuot, Megillat Rut (page 1180) is read before the Torah reading in Shacharit (in Israel, on the first day).

en:Festivals/Amida for Yom Tov:72.en: If the first day of Sukkot falls on Shabbat, then Kohelet (page 1202) is read before the Torah reading in Shacharit on Shemini Atzeret (in Israel, on the first day of Sukkot). Otherwise it is read on Shabbat Chol HaMo'ed.

parts.text: All the Torah scrolls are taken from the Ark.
please answer us on the day we cry.
The Torah scrolls are returned to the Ark except for those used in the Torah Reading.

In Ma’ariv, three (in some congregations, five) are called up and the “VeZot HaBerakha” Torah portion ( pages 1161–1162) is read. See law 136. During Shaḥarit, the prevalent custom is to call up every adult male in the congregation. See law 139.
On Erev Yom Tov, Minḥa begins on page 206. On Shabbat Ḥol HaMo’ed, or when Yom Tov falls on Shabbat, Ma’ariv begins with Psalm 92 on page 324.
When Yom Tov falls on a weekday, Ma’ariv begins with Barekhu on page 334; when Ḥol HaMo’ed falls on a weekday, Ma’ariv begins with “He is compassionate” on page 242.
The following Amida is said in Shaḥarit, Minḥa and Ma’ariv on Yom Tov Pesaḥ, Shavuot, Sukkot, Shemini Atzeret and Simḥat Torah, but not on Ḥol HaMo’ed.
נְקַדֵּשׁ We will sanctify Your name on earth,
as they sanctify it in the highest heavens,
“And they [the angels] call to one another saying:

▴holy is the LORD of hosts the whole world is filled with His glory.”
Then with a sound of mighty noise,

▴“Blessed is the LORD’s glory from His place.”
Reveal Yourself from Your place,
for we are waiting for You. When will You reign in Zion? May it be soon in our days,
and may You dwell there for ever and all time. May You be exalted and sanctified in the midst of Jerusalem,
from generation to generation for evermore. May our eyes see Your kingdom,
as is said in the songs of Your splendor,
written by David your righteous anointed one:
“▴The <small>LORD</small> shall reign for ever. He is your God,
From generation to generation we will declare Your greatness,
and we will proclaim Your holiness for evermore. Your praise,
shall not leave our mouth forever,
are a great and holy King. Blessed are You,

with feet together. If there is a minyan, the Amida is repeated aloud by the Leader.
Take three steps forward and at the points indicated by , bend the knees at the first word, bow at the second, and stand straight before saying God’s name.

He causes the dew to fall.

as is written by Your prophet:

pardon of sin and forgiveness of iniquity

From Marḥeshvan to Adar II in a Jewish leap year (see page 1332)

and atonement of transgression).
For You have chosen Your people Israel from all nations,

and have instituted for them rules for the New Moon.
Blessed are You,
who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons.
During the Leader’s Repetition, the congregation says quietly:
for You are the Lord our God and God of our ancestors,
who formed us and formed the universe. Blessings and thanks are due to Your great and holy name for giving us life and sustaining us. May You continue to give us life and sustain us;
and may You gather our exiles to Your holy courts,
do Your will and serve You with a perfect heart,
for it is for us to give You thanks. Blessed be God to whom thanks­giving is due.</small>
עַל הַנִּסִּים [We thank You also] for the miracles,
and the victories in battle which You performed for our ancestors in those days,

at this time.
בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָֽהוּ In the days of Mattityahu,

the wicked Greek kingdom rose up against Your people Israel to make them forget Your Torah and to force them to transgress the statutes of Your will. It was then that You in Your great compassion stood by them in the time of their distress. You championed their cause,
and avenged their wrong. You delivered the strong into the hands of the weak,
the many into the hands of the few,
the impure into the hands of the pure,
the wicked into the hands of the righteous,
and the arrogant into the hands of those who were engaged in the study of Your Torah. You made for Yourself great and holy renown in Your world,
and for Your people Israel You performed a great salvation and redemption as of this very day. Your children then entered the holiest part of Your House,
kindled lights in Your holy courts,
and designated these eight days of Ḥanukka for giving thanks and praise to Your great name.
The following is said by the Leader during the Repetition of the Amida. In Israel, if Kohanim bless the congregation, turn to page 838. See laws 370–377.
Our God and God of our fathers,
bless us with the threefold blessing in the Torah,
written by the hand of Moses Your servant and pronounced by Aaron and his sons the priests,

as it is said:
May the Lord bless you and protect you.

May it be Your will.
May the Lord make His face shine on you and be gracious to you.

May it be Your will.
May the Lord turn His face toward you,
The following verse concludes the Leader’s Repetition of the Amida.
Some also say it here as part of the silent Amida. See law 368.
On Shavuot, after the Kohen is called up to the Torah and before he makes the blessing,
the following is said responsively by the Reader and the congregation.

The beginning of words – the opening of speech:
I shall ask permission and leave to begin.
Trembling I open my mouth with two matters and three,
by leave of the One who bears us through to old age.
which could not be laid out in words,
If all the seas were ink,
He summoned forth all creation in those six days;
to sit upon His throne of fire.

A heavenly host of a thousand thousands and myriads serve Him –
created each morning anew,
and stand in utter silence until they have leave.

They receive leave from each other –
and at once,
Like a voice from the Almighty,

like the noise of many waters –
Cherubim raise themselves towards the Ophanim in a roar of noise,
to see face to face what looks like sparks of the rainbow flying,
they arrive in a flash of motion.
They bless His glory in every secret term,
from the place of the home of His Presence,
And all the hosts of heaven give praises in great fear,
of the sovereignty that will last through all ages,
They each lay out His holiness in praise,

and when their moment has passed
it is gone forever;
seven years will go by and it will not return.
and they will tell the wonders of His praise in speech.
He desires and values and yearns for them to labor for Him to weariness,
it is their pleas that are fulfilled.
with a crown and an oath,
and worn with the phylacteries He binds to Himself always,
which are inscribed inside with wisdom and with insight,
praise the Master of the Universe,
and it befits me to speak of Him to those of other nations,
that you let yourselves be killed for Him in the lions' den?

if you bent yourselves to our rule:
your will would be done then wherever you would be."
With wisdom I reply to them,

telling them of the end –
"If you only knew,
if you only truly knew Him,
"and what your greatness is worth when compared to that glory,

or the greatness
I will be granted when my salvation comes...
when His presence is revealed to me in might and in great pride."
He shall pay His enemies back in kind,
and perform justice for the beloved people,
when He brings the exiles back into the city of Jerusalem.
He shall cast His glory over them day and night,
as a canopy where they shall voice the splendor in joyful songs,

for the shining of those clouds will make each canopy fine
as the actions of the one who sits in it;
so will each shelter be made.

sit the righteous
in their places before the One whose acts are manifold.
And they appear as seven tiers of joy,
like the dome of the sky in its brilliance,
This is a glory no mouth can express,
glory that the prophets never heard or saw in their visions.
For no eye has ever overseen the Garden of Eden,
where the righteous circle the place of the dance,
and the holy Presence among them.

"It is He!
"The One for whom we longed when we were captives,
"And He will lead us in both worlds;
and He will lead us dancing,
set aside from the beginning of the world for us."

with the Behemoth of the
high mountain,
and when they wrestle one another in their great duel,
the horns of the great Behemoth will gore,
and the mighty Leviathan will leap out at him with his fins,
his Creator will step forward with His great sword,
And they shall sit at tables of rubies and gems,
with rivers of balsam flowing before them,

and quench their thirst in luxury with overflowing cups
of the wondrous wine stored up for them since the first days of creation.
as you have heard the praises in this song,
so may you be promised a place in those joyous circles.
And may you merit to sit in those heavenly rows,
Our God is in the highest heights,
